# Remote Model Inference {#sec-inference}

![Optional remote inference, dynamic view. Source: `docs/adr/architecture/05-remote-inference-flow.mmd`.](../../adr/architecture/rendered/05-remote-inference-flow.png){#fig-inference width=92%}

## Request path on the workstation

`POST /v1/infer/global` and `POST /v1/infer/lesion-roi` both call `infer()` in `dr_support/api/_factory.py`:

1. The image must be admitted and `is_inference_eligible`. Otherwise the API returns `409 Image needs review before analysis`.
2. `mock-*` model IDs are allowed only on `SYNTHETIC` images.
3. `DerivativeService.analysis_image(source)` prepares a deterministic **analysis representation**:
   - `analysis-source-v1` for JPEG and PNG, which pass through unchanged;
   - `analysis-tiff-png-rgb-v1` for TIFF;
   - `analysis-dicom-png-rgb-v1` for DICOM.

   The analysis image has its own SHA-256 and a `CoordinateMapping` back to the original pixels. A payload whose base64 encoding exceeds 20 MB returns `413`; it is never downscaled silently.
4. A process-wide `RLock` serialises provider calls.
5. `RemoteGlobalProvider` / `RemoteLesionProvider` (`providers/remote.py`) POST the base64 analysis image and metadata to the Model API. Details:
   - optional `Authorization: Bearer <REMOTE_MODEL_TOKEN>`;
   - 30 s inference timeout and 5 s metadata timeout;
   - no redirects;
   - responses are validated against the result schemas.
6. Lesion boxes are mapped back to original-image pixels (`map_lesion_result_to_review`).
7. `save_result` stores the raw result and the `analysis_derivative` audit record, and appends an `INFERENCE` event with `source_sha256`, `analysis_sha256`, `transform_id`, runtime, and latency. A new **global** result resets the grade decision to `PENDING` so that a stale human grade never sits beside a new suggestion.

Errors are mapped to plain HTTP codes: `503` (remote not configured), `504` (timeout), `502` (remote error), `409` / `413` (derivative problems).

## Source SHA versus analysis SHA

| Identity | What it hashes | Where it appears |
|:---------|:---------------|:-----------------|
| **Source SHA-256** | The admitted original bytes. This is the case identity and never changes. | Admission record, `images.csv` `image_sha256`, display headers `X-Source-SHA256`, Models & Audit |
| **Analysis SHA-256** | The exact bytes sent to the model (possibly converted). | `analysis_derivative`, `INFERENCE` events, Models & Audit |
| Display derivative SHA | The browser-safe representation served by `/v1/images/{id}/display`. | `ETag` and `X-Derivative-SHA256` headers |

: Image identities. {#tbl-identities tbl-colwidths="[24,40,36]"}

For JPEG and PNG, the analysis bytes equal the source bytes, so both hashes match. TIFF and DICOM produce a different analysis SHA. The mapping keeps every coordinate in original-image pixel space.

## Model API (GPU host)

`dr_support/services/model_api.py` validates the Bearer token with a constant-time comparison when `REMOTE_MODEL_TOKEN` is set, checks the runtime and admission fields, and runs the local providers under a lock.

- **RETFound** (`providers/retfound.py`, model ID `retfound-aptos5`)
  - Pinned source revision and checkpoint SHA-256.
  - Returns a five-class grade suggestion with a softmax score. The score is **uncalibrated**.
- **PRISM-DR** (`providers/prism.py`, model ID `prism-dr-5fold`)
  - ROI cropper, then green-channel median and CLAHE preprocessing.
  - MA/HE/EX run on 1280 px tiles with 0.25 overlap; SE runs on the full image.
  - Five-fold ensemble; boxes are returned in original pixels.
  - The raw output is kept intact. `presentation.py` derives a bounded display subset (`REVIEW_MAX_PER_CLASS`, default 25; `REVIEW_MAX_TOTAL`, default 80) with stable `ai-<20 hex>` detection IDs.

Empty detections never mean "no lesion". The UI and documentation must keep saying so.
